items.title: Profit, loss and base
items.content: Profit = SP − CP when SP > CP; loss = CP − SP when CP > SP. Profit% and loss% are calculated on cost price: \(\text{profit}/CP\times100\%\), \(\text{loss}/CP\times100\%\).

items.title: Discount and marked price
items.content: Discount = MP − SP; discount% is based on marked price. For discount \(d\%\), \(SP=MP(1-d/100)\). Apply successive discounts multiplicatively.

items.title: Exam checks
items.content:
Write CP, SP and MP separately before calculating.
Check that a positive discount lowers the selling price.

items.title: Cost price and selling price
items.content: CP is purchase cost; SP is sale price. Worked example: buy for ₹500 and sell for ₹575; profit = ₹75.

items.title: Profit percentage
items.content: Worked example: CP ₹800, SP ₹920. Profit ₹120; profit% \(=120/800\times100=15\%\).

items.title: Loss percentage
items.content: Worked example: CP ₹1,200, SP ₹1,020. Loss ₹180; loss% \(=180/1200\times100=15\%\).

items.title: Marked price and discount
items.content: Worked example: MP ₹2,000 with 15% discount gives SP \(2000(0.85)=₹1,700\).

items.title: Successive discounts
items.content: Worked example: 20% then 10% off ₹1,000 gives \(1000(0.8)(0.9)=₹720\), an overall 28% discount.

items.title: Find a required selling price
items.content: Worked example: CP ₹640 and target profit 25% require SP \(640(1.25)=₹800\).

items.title: Tax, overhead and net cost
items.content: Include stated costs in CP when the problem defines them as seller’s cost; read whether delivery, tax or commission is included. Worked example: purchase ₹500 plus ₹20 delivery gives CP ₹520; at SP ₹600, profit is ₹80.

items.title: Find profit/loss and rate
items.content: Worked example: CP ₹750, SP ₹690; loss ₹60 and loss rate \(60/750\times100=8\%\).

items.title: Find CP or SP from a rate
items.content: Worked example: SP ₹1,080 at 20% profit means \(SP=1.2CP\), so CP = ₹900.

items.title: Find marked price after discount
items.content: Worked example: SP ₹765 after 15% discount is 85% of MP; MP \(=765/0.85=₹900\).

items.title: Compare discount offers
items.content: Calculate final prices on the same marked price; successive reductions compound. Worked example: on ₹1,000, 20% off gives ₹800; 10% off gives ₹900, so the first offer saves more.

items.title: Multi-step trade problem
items.content: Track each purchase/sale and fee. Calculate net gain from total revenue minus total cost, then use total cost as the percentage base. Worked example: buy 10 items at ₹20 and sell at ₹25 each; cost ₹200, revenue ₹250, profit ₹50 = 25% of cost.

items.title: Derive selling price at profit rate
items.content: If profit is \(p\%\) of CP, then \(SP=CP+CP(p/100)=CP(1+p/100)\).

items.title: Derive selling price after loss
items.content: If loss is \(l\%\) of CP, then \(SP=CP(1-l/100)\).

items.title: Derive successive discounts
items.content: A first discount leaves fraction \(1-d_1/100\); a second leaves \(1-d_2/100\) of that. The combined multiplier is their product.

sections.title: Common errors and how to avoid them

items.title: Wrong percentage base
items.content: Profit/loss percentage uses CP; discount percentage uses MP.

items.title: Confusing discount with profit
items.content: A shop discount is measured from MP; profit compares SP with CP.

items.title: Adding successive discounts
items.content: Apply the second discount to the reduced price, not the original MP.

items.title: Ignoring expenses
items.content: Include costs specified in the problem before calculating net profit.

keyTakeaways: Profit and loss compare selling price with cost price.
Profit/loss percentage uses cost price as base.
Discount percentage uses marked price as base.

questionTypes: Find CP or SP from a rate
proofsAndDerivations: Derive selling price at profit rate
